# Overview

This tutorial runs the two Zentangler mediation models on the ASD multi-omics
example data, both through the main entry point `zentangler()`:

1. `zentangler(mae, x_var = ..., y_var = ...)` (default `model = "parallel"`)
   for pure parallel mediation.
2. `zentangler(mae, model = "sequential", x_var = ..., y_var = ..., route = c(...))`
   for one explicit sequential route.

These dispatch to `fit_multiview_parallel_zentangler()` and
`fit_sequential_zentangler()`, which can also be called directly and whose help
pages list every option.

The ASD example uses a time contrast as the exposure:

```text
X = 0 at baseline T0
X = 1 at follow-up T1
```

and one symptom score as the outcome.

# Packages

```{r}
library(Zentangler)
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
```

# Load The ASD Data

The tutorial uses the ASD files in `data/`. If you run this from another
working directory, set `ZENTANGLER_DATA_DIR` to the folder containing the ASD
`.RData` files.

```{r}
helper_file <- c(
  "asd-data-helpers.R",
  file.path("vignettes", "asd-data-helpers.R")
)
helper_file <- helper_file[file.exists(helper_file)][[1]]
source(helper_file)

asd <- load_asd_example_data()
names(asd$omics)
```

# Build One ASD MultiAssayExperiment

Here we build a `MultiAssayExperiment` for the `T1` contrast and the `ABC`
symptom outcome.

```{r}
mae_t1_abc <- build_asd_mae(
  omics = asd$omics,
  symptoms = asd$symptoms,
  contrast = "T1",
  symptom = "ABC"
)

mae_t1_abc
```

# 1. Pure Parallel Zentangler

The parallel API treats all selected mediators as candidate routes of the form:

```text
X -> mediator -> Y
```

There are no mediator-to-mediator links in this model. The default outcome
model is multiview cooperative learning (`fusion = "multiview"`), whose
agreement parameter `rho` runs from 0 (early fusion) to 1 (late fusion) and is
chosen by cross-validation; this quick tutorial run uses the supplementary
IntegratedLearner-style early fusion.

```{r}
parallel_fit <- zentangler(
  mae_t1_abc,
  x_var = "X",
  y_var = "Y",
  sis_n = 25,
  fusion = "integrated_learner",
  integrated_learner_fusion = "early",
  y_family = "gaussian",
  fdr_method = "BH",
  fdr_scope = "global",
  fill_nonfinite_zero = TRUE,
  seed = 1
)

parallel_summary <- summary(parallel_fit, q_threshold = 0.25)
parallel_summary$model
parallel_summary$views
zentangler_mediators(parallel_fit, top = 10)
```

# 2. One Sequential Route

The sequential API runs one ordered route. For example:

```text
X -> species -> fecal_metabolites -> Y
```

The first layer is screened by exposure association. Adjacent layers are
screened by mediator-to-mediator correlation, and retained links are refit by
regression. The route is passed as an ordered character vector of view names
(`route`). The terminal outcome model uses multiview cooperative learning by
default (`fusion = "multiview"`, each route layer is one view, `rho` in
\[0, 1\] chosen by cross-validation); IntegratedLearner-style early fusion
(`fusion = "integrated_learner"`, `integrated_learner_fusion = "early"`) is the
supplementary single-model alternative and is used below to keep the tutorial
fast.

```{r}
sequential_fit <- zentangler(
  mae_t1_abc,
  model = "sequential",
  x_var = "X",
  y_var = "Y",
  route = c("species", "fecal_metabolites"),
  sis_n = 25,
  cor_method = "spearman",
  min_abs_cor = 0.15,
  cor_q_threshold = 0.5,
  fusion = "integrated_learner",
  integrated_learner_fusion = "early",
  lambda_choice = "lambda.min",
  y_family = "gaussian",
  seed = 1
)

species_fecal_paths <- zentangler_paths(sequential_fit)
sequential_fit$settings$route
head(species_fecal_paths, 20)
summary(sequential_fit)$model
head(sequential_fit$edges, 20)
head(sequential_fit$terminals, 20)
zentangler_effects(sequential_fit)
```

# 3. Additional Sequential Route Scenarios

The ASD example has four modalities:

```{r}
names(asd$omics)
```

Because the sequential API fits one explicit ordered route at a time, different
biological hypotheses are run as separate fits. The helper below keeps the call
consistent across scenarios.

```{r}
run_asd_sequential_route <- function(route_name, route_views, sis_n = 25) {
  fit <- fit_sequential_zentangler(
    mae_t1_abc,
    x_var = "X",
    y_var = "Y",
    route = route_views,
    sis_n = sis_n,
    cor_method = "spearman",
    min_abs_cor = 0.15,
    cor_q_threshold = 0.5,
    fusion = "integrated_learner",
    integrated_learner_fusion = "early",
    lambda_choice = "lambda.min",
    glmnet_alpha = 0.5,
    y_family = "gaussian",
    seed = 1
  )

  paths <- zentangler_paths(fit)
  if (nrow(paths) > 0) {
    paths$route_name <- route_name
    paths$view_route <- paste(route_views, collapse = " -> ")
    paths <- paths[
      ,
      c("route_name", "view_route", setdiff(names(paths), c("route_name", "view_route"))),
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  }

  list(
    fit = fit,
    paths = paths,
    model = summary(fit)$model
  )
}
```

Here are several two-modality and three-modality routes using the same four ASD
views.

```{r}
asd_route_scenarios <- list(
  species_to_kos = c("species", "kos"),
  species_to_fecal = c("species", "fecal_metabolites"),
  species_to_plasma = c("species", "plasma_metabolites"),
  kos_to_fecal = c("kos", "fecal_metabolites"),
  kos_to_plasma = c("kos", "plasma_metabolites"),
  fecal_to_plasma = c("fecal_metabolites", "plasma_metabolites"),
  species_to_kos_to_fecal = c("species", "kos", "fecal_metabolites"),
  species_to_kos_to_plasma = c("species", "kos", "plasma_metabolites")
)

asd_route_fits <- Map(
  run_asd_sequential_route,
  names(asd_route_scenarios),
  asd_route_scenarios
)

route_models <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(asd_route_fits), function(route_name) {
    out <- asd_route_fits[[route_name]]$model
    out$route_name <- route_name
    out$view_route <- paste(asd_route_scenarios[[route_name]], collapse = " -> ")
    out[, c("route_name", "view_route", setdiff(names(out), c("route_name", "view_route"))), drop = FALSE]
  })
)

route_path_list <- Filter(
  function(x) is.data.frame(x) && nrow(x) > 0,
  lapply(asd_route_fits, `[[`, "paths")
)
route_paths <- if (length(route_path_list) > 0) do.call(rbind, route_path_list) else data.frame()

route_models
if (nrow(route_paths) > 0) {
  head(route_paths[order(route_paths$q_primary, route_paths$p_primary), ], 20)
} else {
  route_paths
}
```

Each layer of a route is one view of the MAE. To treat several views as one
biological layer (for example `species` and `kos` as a microbiome layer), combine
their features into a single experiment before building the MAE, and then use
that experiment as one element of `route`.

# 4. Sequential Diagnostics and Bootstrap

The sequential API exposes the same kind of layers as the parallel API:
complete paths, retained mediator-to-mediator edges, terminal B-stage effects,
post-selection causal-effect summaries, and run diagnostics.

```{r}
sequential_fit$diagnostics
```

For uncertainty on the full path score, use `path_inference = "bootstrap_score"`:
every replicate re-runs route discovery, and the path p-value is the sign-based
bootstrap p-value of the path score. `causal_inference = "bootstrap"` adds
bootstrap intervals to the causal effects of the fixed set of significant
paths. Increase
`bootstrap_repeats` for real analysis; the small value below is only for a quick
tutorial run.

```{r}
sequential_boot_fit <- fit_sequential_zentangler(
  mae_t1_abc,
  x_var = "X",
  y_var = "Y",
  route = c("species", "fecal_metabolites"),
  sis_n = 12,
  cor_method = "spearman",
  min_abs_cor = 0.15,
  cor_q_threshold = 0.75,
  fusion = "integrated_learner",
  integrated_learner_fusion = "early",
  lambda_choice = "lambda.min",
  b_inference = "debiased",
  path_inference = "bootstrap_score",
  causal_inference = "bootstrap",
  bootstrap_repeats = 5,
  y_family = "gaussian",
  seed = 1
)

head(zentangler_paths(sequential_boot_fit), 20)
zentangler_effects(sequential_boot_fit)
```

# Save Results

```{r}
out_dir <- file.path("tutorial_results", "asd_sequential_zentangler")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

write.csv(
  zentangler_mediators(parallel_fit),
  file.path(out_dir, "parallel_all_mediators.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  species_fecal_paths,
  file.path(out_dir, "sequential_species_to_fecal_paths.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  route_models,
  file.path(out_dir, "sequential_route_scenario_model_summaries.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  route_paths,
  file.path(out_dir, "sequential_route_scenario_paths.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  list(
    parallel_fit = parallel_fit,
    sequential_fit = sequential_fit,
    asd_route_fits = asd_route_fits,
    sequential_boot_fit = sequential_boot_fit
  ),
  file.path(out_dir, "asd_sequential_zentangler_fits.rds")
)
```

# Interpreting The Output

For sequential route fits, the main path table includes:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `route_type` | `sequential` |
| `mediator_path` | feature-level mediator path |
| `a` | exposure-to-first-mediator coefficient |
| `d_product` | product of mediator-to-mediator link coefficients |
| `b` | terminal mediator-to-outcome coefficient |
| `sequential_score` | `a * d_product * b` |
| `p_primary` | conservative path-level screening p-value |
| `q_primary` | global FDR-adjusted path-level value |
| `in_effect_set` | path enters the causal-effect stage (`q_primary <= effect_q_threshold`) |

The terminal outcome model of the fit is stored in `summary(sequential_fit)$model`
(`fusion`, and the chosen `rho` for the multiview model). Use
`zentangler_paths(sequential_fit, q_threshold = 0.25)` for the active paths and
`zentangler_paths(sequential_fit, top = 20)` for the top-ranked paths.

Sequential fits also expose a post-selection causal-effect layer through
`sequential_fit$effects`, `zentangler_effects(sequential_fit)`, and
`summary(sequential_fit)$effects`.

For the pure parallel model, use the usual Zentangler helpers:

```{r}
head(zentangler_mediators(parallel_fit))
summary(parallel_fit, q_threshold = seq(0.05, 0.25, by = 0.05))$thresholds
```
